Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Combat HUD

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The editable HUD scene restores the original health plate, three cooldown pips, draining status squares, large magazine display, Titan health bar and nearby-teammate revive prompt. It shares the copied steel theme with the counter. The scene owns layout and node lifetime; scripts/hud.odin supplies values.

The game's adapter passes the predicted local player and tick plus the confirmed world into the HUD each frame. Health, ammunition, ability cooldowns and dash readiness therefore follow the same local state as the runner. Boss health and downed-teammate eligibility use confirmed state; the local revive hold displays its progress. A spectator sees the boss bar without personal health/ammo panels. The HUD retains neither a world nor a Session and makes no gameplay decisions.

Health drains and changes color, including the plate's increased maximum. Q/E and Shift pips consume/refill through ordinary casts and dashes; status squares use catalog colors and remaining duration. The magazine distinguishes ready, low, jammed and reloading states, rises above the counter during a floor clear, and returns to its authored offsets on descent. The boss bar hides on death.

Original dimensions/colors/texture regions come from the original ui/hud.tscn and scripts/hud.odin. This port labels its selected ability slots Q/E and its revive key F. The boss plate sits below the existing selected-ability name line; the prompt adds hold progress. These are authored adaptations rather than a pixel-identical HUD claim. Fill extents and magazine offsets are cached from the scene at ready, so editing those dimensions does not require renderer constants.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/hud_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_HUD_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/output/directory \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/hud_run.sh

The gate drives the actual game in the workbench: preparation uses admitted development actions, then normal firing, casts, dash, purchases and boss combat exercise the displays. revive_run.sh checks the prompt across a multiplayer hold/cancel/completion, and run_loop.sh checks magazine placement across clears and descent. Existing workbench and shop gates remain runnable.

See evidence. Native captures use Dummy audio because the local CoreAudio issue remains open. Run transitions are now implemented. Browser interaction, additional platforms, listening/feel comparisons and broader UI parity remain work. The downed-player camera is now implemented and tested separately. The full roadmap is not completed by this HUD slice.
